name: West Ridge
descent_text: Reverse the ridge to La Bohn Lakes. The rock on the ridge is loose, with blocks that shift underfoot, so test holds and keep clear of other parties. From the lakes, drop back to Necklace Valley either by the heather and cairn line along the tree line or by the boulder gully and stream below La Bohn Gap, which is mostly class 2; in early season the snow chute to the gap needs an ice axe and often crampons. Then follow Necklace Valley trail down past the lakes, the steep 2,400 ft switchbacks and the footlog, and out the flat five miles to the trailhead.
approach: Park at the Necklace Valley (East Fork Foss) trailhead at the end of FR 68 and follow the East Fork Foss trail up the valley. The first five miles are gentle forest, gaining only about 600 ft, until a footlog crossing of the East Fork Foss River, then the trail climbs about 2,400 ft in three miles of steep, rooty switchbacks to Jade Lake and on up the Necklace Valley past the other lakes. Leave the valley trail at its upper end, where the hanging valley leads to La Bohn Lakes and the climb proper. Camps at the lakes or in Necklace Valley make this a two-day trip for most parties. From the end of the valley, hug the tree line left, following cairns up heather to the outlet of the lower La Bohn Lake, then continue to the upper lake; the ridge above it is the start of the climb.
overview: Many variations work. One typical plan: get to La Bohn gap (a bit below 6k feet), ascend the Hinman Glacier onto the west ridge, and then traverse the glacier's upper margin, which goes on surprisingly long but is enjoyable.
